taxonomy:
Here is a taxonomy of the listed grid-based logic games, using only the rule descriptions provided.

## 1. Loop-drawing puzzles
These require drawing one continuous loop through cells or dots.

- **Dotchi-Loop** — single loop through cell centers; must pass white circles and avoid black circles.
- **Masyu** — single loop through cell centers; passes through black and white circles with turn/straight constraints.
- **Mid-loop** — single loop through cells; must pass through all black circles as midpoints of straight segments.
- **Moon-or-Sun** — single loop through cells; must visit rooms in an alternating moon/sun pattern.
- **Nagareru** — single directional loop; arrows determine the loop’s direction and wind affects movement.
- **Suraromu** — single loop through cells; must pass all gates in a specified order from a numbered start.
- **Yajilin** — single loop through cells; numbers indicate black cells in arrow directions.
- **Slitherlink** — single loop along grid edges around numbered cells.
- **Numberlink** — connect matching number pairs with non-crossing lines.
- **Hebi** — snake-number paths 1 to 5 in white cells, with directional constraints from black cells.

## 2. Shading / coloring puzzles
These ask you to color cells black/white or shaded/unshaded under structural constraints.

- **Akari** — place light bulbs in white cells so all white cells are illuminated.
- **Hitori** — blacken cells so numbers don’t repeat in rows/columns; white cells stay connected.
- **Kurodoko** — blacken cells so numbered cells see the correct number of white cells.
- **Kurotto** — color cells so circles match the sum of continuous black cells extending from them.
- **Nurikabe** — blacken cells to form a connected wall with no 2×2 black area.
- **Nurimeizu** — paint cells to form walls and a maze from S to G.
- **Nurimisaki** — fill cells so marked cells become “Misaki” promontories with straight-line counts.
- **Norinori** — place blocks in pairs in consecutive black squares.
- **Usowan** — color cells so each region has exactly one wrong number.
- **Sto-stone** — color cells so room black-cell counts match and dropped stones fill the lower half.
- **Tilepaint** — color tiles so the final pattern outlines an object.
- **Shakashaka** — place black triangles in squares so remaining white areas form rectangles/squares.
- **LITS** — color tetrominoes in each region with connectivity and no 2×2 black blocks.
- **Nuritwin** — shade cells so each region contains exactly two same-sized blocks.
- **Choco Banana** — paint some cells black so black and white areas satisfy shape constraints.
- **Double Choco** — divide into blocks containing matching white and gray areas.
- **Chained Block** — fill cells black/unknown so blocks form chains with shape uniqueness constraints.

## 3. Number-placement puzzles
These require filling cells with numbers according to local or regional rules.

- **Fillomino** — divide board into same-number blocks whose size matches the number.
- **Five Cells** — divide grid into blocks of five cells with line-count clues.
- **Makaro** — fill rooms with numbers; arrows point to the largest adjacent number.
- **Nansuke** — fill blank cells with numbers from a given list.
- **Ripple Effect** — fill rooms with consecutive numbers starting from 1, with spacing rules for repeats.
- **Shikaku** — divide grid into rectangles, each containing one number equal to rectangle size.
- **Sudoku** — fill 1–9 so rows, columns, and 3×3 blocks contain all digits.
- **Juosan** — fill cells with horizontal or vertical marks under territory count rules.
- **Sashigane** — divide grid into L-shaped blocks with size and marker constraints.
- **Satogaeri** — move circles so each country contains one circle; movement length may be constrained.
- **Pencils** — mark pencils and draw lines from tips using pencil-length numbers.
- **Evolomino** — place squares in blocks that evolve by adding one square along arrow routes.

## 4. Bridge / network connection puzzles
These involve connecting nodes or regions with bridges or paths.

- **Hashiwokakero** — connect islands with bridges matching island numbers.
- **Numberlink** — connect matching numbers with continuous lines.
- **Yosenabe** — move circles into gray areas so area sums match circle values.
- **Satogaeri** — move circles through tracks into countries without crossing.
- **Nuritwin** — shaded cells must connect across region boundaries.
- **Double Choco** — blocks are formed by pairing matching shapes of white and gray areas.

## 5. Region partitioning puzzles
These focus on dividing the grid into regions with specific shapes or contents.

- **Shikaku** — rectangles containing one number.
- **Fillomino** — blocks of equal numbers with size matching the number.
- **Five Cells** — blocks of exactly five cells.
- **Chained Block** — black-cell blocks with chain constraints.
- **Double Choco** — blocks containing paired same-form areas.
- **Nuritwin** — regions containing exactly two same-sized blocks.
- **Sashigane** — L-shaped blocks.
- **LITS** — tetromino blocks in bounded areas.
- **Moon-or-Sun** — rooms with moon-only or sun-only traversal.
- **Heyawake** — rooms with painted-cell counts and white-cell connectivity constraints.
- **Makaro** — rooms containing all numbers up to room size.
- **Sto-stone** — rooms with black-cell counts and gravity behavior.
- **Nurimeizu** — rooms that are uniformly painted or white.
- **Shakashaka** — white remainder must form rectangles/squares.

## 6. Adjacency / visibility / counting puzzles
These rely on counting neighboring cells, visible cells, or directional counts.

- **Akari** — numbers count adjacent bulbs; bulbs illuminate along rows/columns.
- **Kurodoko** — numbers count visible white cells to nearest black cell/frame.
- **Kurotto** — circles count continuous black cells extending in four directions.
- **Hebi** — black-cell arrows count nearest snake cell in arrow direction.
- **Makaro** — arrows point to the largest adjacent number.
- **Usowan** — numbers count adjacent colored cells, with one wrong number per region.
- **Yajilin** — numbers count black cells in arrow direction.
- **Ripple Effect** — repeated numbers in rows/columns must be spaced apart by at least the number.
- **Juosan** — counts horizontal/vertical marks in territories.
- **Shakashaka** — numbers count surrounding black triangles.
- **Slitherlink** — numbers count surrounding line segments.
- **Five Cells** — numbers count surrounding block lines.
- **Suraromu** — gate numbers determine crossing order.
- **Nagareru** — wind and arrow direction constrain loop movement.

## 7. Snake / path-sequence puzzles
These involve ordered sequences or directional progression.

- **Hebi** — snakes are sequences from 1 to 5.
- **Evolomino** — blocks evolve by adding one square along arrow routes.
- **Pencils** — lines extend from pencil tips through numbered lengths.
- **Satogaeri** — circles move along tracks into countries.
- **Suraromu** — loop starts at a numbered circle and crosses gates in order.
- **Nagareru** — loop direction is determined by arrows and wind.
- **Moon-or-Sun** — loop alternates room content types as it moves.

## 8. Shape-matching / polyomino puzzles
These depend on matching shapes, sizes, or polyomino forms.

- **Choco Banana** — black and white areas in a block must match in form.
- **Double Choco** — white and gray areas in a block must match in form.
- **LITS** — tetrominoes in each region; same-shaped tetrominoes cannot touch.
- **Evolomino** — later blocks must be previous blocks plus one square, same orientation.
- **Chained Block** — blocks are compared by size and shape within chains.
- **Nuritwin** — each region contains two same-sized blocks.
- **Sashigane** — all blocks are L-shaped.
- **Shikaku** — all regions are rectangles.
- **Shakashaka** — white remainder must be rectangles or squares.
- **Nurimeizu** — rooms are uniformly painted or white.

## 9. Special constraint puzzles
These have distinctive rule sets that don’t fit neatly elsewhere.

- **Heyawake** — white cells cannot stretch across more than two rooms in a straight line.
- **Hitori** — black cells cannot touch; white cells must connect.
- **Nurikabe** — black wall must connect and avoid 2×2 blocks.
- **Nurimisaki** — white cells must form a connected network and avoid 2×2 blocks.
- **Sto-stone** — gravity/dropping rule after coloring.
- **Nagareru** — wind affects loop direction and movement.
- **Suraromu** — gates must all be passed exactly once.
- **Moon-or-Sun** — room-by-room alternation of moon/sun traversal.
- **Usowan** — exactly one wrong number per region.
- **Chained Block** — chain uniqueness by shape.
